topics.title: Meaning, objectives and advantages of ratio analysis

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what an accounting ratio is and why it must relate meaningfully connected figures.
State the objectives for which ratio analysis is carried out.
Identify the advantages of ratio analysis and its indicative, whistle-blowing role.
Explain how limitations of financial statements, such as ignored price-level changes and varied practices, limit ratio analysis.
Identify the limitations of ratios themselves, such as lack of standard definitions and standard levels.
Classify ratios as statement of profit and loss, balance sheet or composite ratios.
Classify ratios as liquidity, solvency, activity or profitability ratios by their purpose.
Calculate and interpret the current ratio.
Calculate and interpret the quick (liquid or acid-test) ratio.
Analyse how a transaction changes the current ratio.
Calculate and interpret the debt-equity ratio.
Calculate the proprietary, debt to capital employed and total assets to debt ratios.
Calculate and interpret the interest coverage ratio.
Calculate and interpret the inventory turnover ratio.
Calculate trade receivables and payables turnover ratios with collection and payment periods.
Interpret net assets, fixed assets and working capital turnover ratios.
Calculate gross profit, operating and net profit ratios.
Calculate and interpret return on investment and return on shareholders' funds.
Calculate earnings per share, book value per share, dividend payout and P/E ratios.
